title.narrative: WGG- Research and Documentation in India

description.narrative: The strategy of research and documentation is integral to the learning and evidence building agenda of the WGG Consortium and its country-level strategic partners. There are significant programmatic components of the consortium wide joint activities as part of global and regional advocacy efforts.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

Target updated for 2024. Partner organizations have proposed position papers on GBV, One stop crisis centre, political participation and women reservation bill and some other reseearch studies and developmentof knowledge prodcucts.

Study and survey of One Stop Crisis Center : The objective was to understand the functioning of the One Stop Center (OSCC) and its effectiveness to ensure that these centers are providing supportive and inclusive services to women, children and persons with disabilities. Under this activity, OSCC, Lucknow was visited along with representatives from various institutions like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, East Singhbhum and CREA, SDRC. A campaign video celebrating 8th March, International Women's Day was produced by SDRC on the topic - "Does Reservation for Women in Election Ensure Political Rights of All Women?” The video compiled voices of young women from different segments of the society, with different socio-economical background, including WWDs.SDRC guided WGG partner organizations to collect information on one stop crisis centers in respective states & prepared the report while the survey was conducted in 4 partner states.Flaws in laws in Hindi, ally ship in Hindi and study was conducted by CREA.

Yuva: Conducted a survey with 110 girls and women regarding access to sanitary pads and problems faced by disabled girls and women during menstruation. The consortium partner has been using the knowledge generated as a result of the survey to do advocacy with the government at state, district and local levels.ASS: A resource material on the issues related to human rights has been prepared by the organiation, and 1000 copies are printed for distribution in various programs on SGBV. GSS: 10 short movies prepared by young leaders for the purpose of doing advocacy on SGBV. Survey conducted to identify disabled women, 10 new disabled women are added to the project.CREA: Prepared three knowledge resource doc in Hindi with the support of other programs in CREA. One brochure on marriage incentive of people with disability , one Hindi document on flaws in laws and one on the article on disability and sexuality in Hindi.

CREA hosted three instititutes(Feminist Leadership and Movement Building and Rights Institite and Disability, Sexuality, Rights Online institute) with 30 participants each(Young women, Women with disabilities, representatives of WROs, activists, and organization leads). CREA also hosted the SELF (Sports, Expression, Leadership, and Freedom) Academy with 30 young girls to increase their knowledge and capacity in local level advocacy on gender equality and elimination of Sexual and Gender Based Violence(SGBV). Partner CSO organization organized a dialogue-meeting with 150 participants at Panchayat, Block and District level on the topics of gender-based violence, social security scheme, mental health, participation in voting, caste and gender. Additionaly, following activities were organized by the partner CSO with YWLs and WWDs- Quarterly Outreach and Advocacy meetings with Non-state duty bearers led by YW&G and WGWDs. 2. Quarterly Outreach and Advocacy meetings with state duty bearers led by YW&G and WGWDs. YW&G and WGWDs also attended local Government community level meeting to ensure inclusion of SGBV as part of the agenda of those meeting. Cross learning visits were conducted 3 times to different institutions including Mahila Police Station, Sadar Hospital, District Legal Services Authority and Gender Resource Centre. Interface meetings were held with the participants on gender-based violence and protection of rights with persons with disabilities, health service providers, Mahila Panchayat representatives and administrative officials at the block level.
